title: Secrets of Scotland Yard
paragraphs: A crime anthology dramatizing notable British cases associated with Scotland Yard, with stories centered on murder, fraud, theft, and the investigative methods used to solve them.

British true-crime anthology built from dramatizations of actual crimes and Scotland Yard investigations. Contemporary evidence documents a 52-part international run by May 1948, while later surviving copies carry Towers of London syndication numbers/dates and a separate 60-entry 1957 package order. These distribution layers are preserved separately rather than forced into one canonical chronology.

GRH documents the program through International transcription run documented in 1948 (May 7, 1948) and Later Mutual U.S. rebroadcast/package era (1957 to 1959) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]].

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include historical true crime and criminal cases, police investigation and Scotland Yard methods, murder and homicide, forensic and physical evidence, fraud, forgery and counterfeiting, and trial, evidence and legal judgment.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Postwar public appetite for true crime, International transcription syndication, Scotland Yard and forensic authority in popular culture, and Later American rebroadcast life.
